comparison: Perfect agreement on neutrophil findings (C5, C6, C39, C41-C43, C51-C53, C62, C67). Both evaluations rate these claims as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the quantitative analysis and positive control validation, while peer reviewers identify this as 'one of the main findings' with no challenges raised.

Perfect agreement on positive control validation (C40, C44, C45). Both evaluations rate these claims as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the morphological distinction between intravascular and extravasated neutrophils, while peer reviewers accept the EIU control as validating the detection method.

Disagreement on mechanistic interpretations (C63-C66). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting they are 'largely speculative interpretations' without direct testing. Peer reviewers rate them as SUPPORTED, accepting them as reasonable frameworks for future investigation without requesting additional experiments.

Perfect agreement on background claims (C1, C2, C7-C12). Both evaluations rate these as SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes them as 'established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations,' while peer reviewers treat them as accepted knowledge motivating the research.

Perfect agreement on future potential (C68). Both evaluations rate this claim as SUPPORTED. OpenEval calls it 'a reasonable extrapolation from demonstrated capabilities,' while peer reviewers explicitly affirm the technology's value and broad appeal.

Perfect agreement on methodological details (C69-C72). Both evaluations rate these as SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes them as 'straightforward factual statements,' while peer reviewers implicitly accept them as appropriate without challenge.

Strong agreement on microglial response (C4, C31-C36, C46-C48, C61). Both evaluations rate these as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes converging evidence from multiple imaging modalities, while peer reviewers describe the findings as 'striking' and providing 'unprecedented view.' Peer R2 also includes C37-C38, C49-C50 which OpenEval evaluates separately.

Strong agreement on lesion model characterization (C3, C13-C23, C27, C73-C74). Both evaluations rate these as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes marginal statistical significance for some temporal data, while peer reviewers praise this as 'one of the major advances' without raising concerns. Peer R1 also includes C24-C26, C54 which OpenEval evaluates separately.

Disagreement on nuclear density recovery mechanism (C55-C57). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, calling the 'spill into' interpretation 'speculative' without direct evidence like cell tracking. Peer reviewers rate them as SUPPORTED, accepting them as part of the lesion characterization without challenge. Partial overlap with C24-C26.

Agreement on temporal sequence findings (C37-C38, C58-C59). OpenEval rates these as SUPPORTED based on temporal imaging data showing hyperreflectivity precedes microglial migration. Peer reviewers also rate them as SUPPORTED, accepting the temporal sequence as part of the 'striking' time-course analysis.

Disagreement on quantitative nuclear density data (C24-C26). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN due to marginal statistical significance (p=0.17, p=0.07) and contradictory implications. Peer R1 includes these claims in their SUPPORTED evaluation of the lesion model without noting statistical concerns.

Agreement on phagocytosis findings (C49-C50). OpenEval rates these as SUPPORTED based on confocal microscopy with quantitative measurements (p<0.001). Peer reviewers include these in their SUPPORTED evaluation of microglial response as part of the 'extremely thorough examination.'

Agreement on hyperreflectivity temporal sequence (C37-C38). OpenEval rates these as SUPPORTED, concluding microglia do not cause initial hyperreflectivity based on temporal data. Peer reviewers include these in their SUPPORTED evaluation of the microglial time-course without challenge.

Agreement on methodological comparison (C54). OpenEval rates this as SUPPORTED based on demonstrated precision and citations to alternative methods. Peer R1 includes this in their SUPPORTED evaluation, with Reviewer 3 noting the model uses 'close to 2 orders of magnitude lower laser power' than alternatives.

Agreement on vascular integrity (C28-C30, C60). OpenEval includes these in SUPPORTED evaluation of confined damage with multiple imaging modalities. Peer R4 rates them as SUPPORTED, affirming the laser 'spares the vasculature' without raising concerns about blood-retinal barrier assessment.
